annotation.title_clean: Surgeon Attitudes Toward AI-Enhanced Robotic Surgery: A Survey on Autonomy, Liability, and Skill Erosion
annotation.title_en: Surgeon Attitudes Toward AI-Enhanced Robotic Surgery: A Survey on Autonomy, Liability, and Skill Erosion
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Taghipour, N.; Mostafavinia, A.; Mehran, H.; Hosseini, S.; Alighadr, A.; Javaherinasab, M.; et al.
annotation.summary_en: Qualitative interview study of 25 Iranian surgeons on AI-enhanced robotic surgery. Surgeons favour assistive and shared-control systems over unsupervised autonomy. They report uncertainty about liability for AI errors and call for Iran-specific regulation. They also fear skill erosion and recommend hybrid and simulation-based training.
key_provisions_or_claims: Surgeons support assistive/shared-control AI but are skeptical of unsupervised autonomy
Liability for AI-driven errors is unclear; participants call for Iran-specific regulatory frameworks
Over-reliance on AI risks deskilling, especially among younger surgeons
Hybrid training and simulation-based learning proposed for skill maintenance
Iranian surgeons show greater concern about affordability, access and legal clarity than international peers
